annotations.description: Bloodline Pretender is a 2/2 with no evasion, while Mistwalker is a 1/4 flyer that starts an evasive clock and blocks Initiate's Companion without dying. The sequencing argument (Pretender now so Mistwalker triggers it next turn) has some merit, but Mistwalker's flying and defensive stats are more immediately impactful.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mistwalker (1/4 flying) for immediate evasive pressure and better defense against Initiate's Companion, then play Pretender next turn

annotations.description: Chose 'Horror' as the creature type for Bloodline Pretender, but no known non-Changeling creatures in the deck or hand are Horrors. Nyxathid (an Elemental) is literally in hand and will be castable soon, so choosing 'Elemental' would guarantee at least one extra +1/+1 counter trigger beyond what Changeling creatures already provide.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose 'Horror' for Bloodline Pretender's creature type
annotations.betterLine: Choose 'Elemental' to synergize with Nyxathid in hand, or another type matching non-Changeling creatures in the deck

annotations.description: Declined to attack with Initiate's Companion (3/1) when the opponent's only available blocker was Wight of Precinct Six (1/1). The opponent is very unlikely to block (trading a growing Wight for a Cat is bad for them), so this would likely deal 3 damage and untap a land via the combat damage trigger. The untapped land could even enable casting Pouncing Cheetah (flash, {2}{G}) in the opponent's turn.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Initiate's Companion. If unblocked, deal 3 damage and untap a land (enabling potential Pouncing Cheetah flash play). If blocked by Wight, trade a 3/1 for a 1/1 which is acceptable.

annotations.description: Not attacking with Bloodline Pretender (3/3) when the opponent's only available blocker is Initiate's Companion (3/1). If the opponent doesn't block, that's 3 free damage. If they trade, it's roughly even. The opponent is at 20 life so pressure matters, and passing up free damage when the opponent may choose not to block is leaving value on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Bloodline Pretender (3/3). The opponent either takes 3 damage or trades their 3/1 Initiate's Companion for it, both of which are acceptable outcomes.

annotations.description: Attacking with Weaselback Redcap (1/1) risks losing the only Goblin on the battlefield, which is needed to sacrifice for Goblin Grenade (5 damage to any target) in hand. annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with both Initiate's Companion and Weaselback Redcap
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Initiate's Companion (3/1), preserving Weaselback Redcap as Goblin Grenade fodder. The 1 extra damage from Redcap is not worth risking the 5-damage Grenade option.

With a flying Mistwalker threatening persistent evasive damage and a growing Bloodline Pretender, removing a key creature would have been far more impactful than dealing face damage in a losing board position.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted GPT53C Detect (opponent's face) with Goblin Grenade for 5 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Target Mistwalker with Goblin Grenade to remove the flying threat that is very difficult to interact with otherwise, helping stabilize the board. Alternatively, target Bloodline Pretender to prevent it from continuing to grow. When behind on board, removal is worth more than face damage.

annotations.description: Casting Heirloom Blade over Pirated Copy when the opponent has no creatures and is at 12 life. This increases board pressure significantly. Heirloom Blade won't be equipped until next turn and doesn't add a creature.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Pirated Copy for 5 mana copying Bloodline Pretender or Wight of Precinct Six to immediately add another threat and increase board pressure while opponent is defenseless
